Taste more. Waste less.

AIN CENTER · THE HEIST · SUSTAINABILITY TRACK

MarketBite turns surplus food into better deals for students. Cafes can adjust prices throughout the day, helping more meals get sold and less food go to waste.

THE PROBLEM WE’RE CRACKING

Food left behind.
Resources lost with it.

An unsold sandwich represents more than the food in the case. Growing its ingredients takes land and water; preparing, refrigerating, and delivering it takes energy and people’s work. When food goes uneaten, those resources have already been used.

Much of food waste’s climate impact happens before disposal, through production, processing, and transport. Preventing waste can protect the value of those resources. Why food waste matters ↗

MarketBite starts with a practical campus opportunity: connect surplus inventory to timely, responsible price drops so more prepared food finds a buyer. Our goal is less unsold food and more affordable meals. A future pilot would compare unsold quantities and discarded food against a baseline, alongside student savings and cafe revenue.

THE PEOPLE BEHIND MARKETBITE

Built at Rochester.

Campus food waste felt close to home. As Rochester students, we wanted to address food left unsold in the places we visit every day, while helping more students afford a meal.

Over the ten-day Ain Center’s The Heist Hackathon, we brought together product design, software, business, and sustainability research to turn that problem into MarketBite.

Our idea pairs the familiarity of a campus cafe with a live food market: prices respond to stock and time, and timely alerts give students a reason to stop by before surplus goes to waste. Connections Cafe became the setting for our prototype.

We’re entering the Sustainability track with a shared aim: less unsold food and more affordable meals. The Ain Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation helps students develop ideas into ventures through hands-on programs, mentoring, and competitions.

    OUR AIM / LESS WASTE, MORE POSSIBILITY

    Good food.
    Fewer leftovers.

    Help prepared food find a buyer while making campus meals more affordable. Start with what is in the case, and make every decision count.

    01 / FOOD

    Keep good food moving.

    Timely offers can connect unsold food with people who want it. Inventory and approved selling windows guide what reaches the menu.

    02 / WATER & ENERGY

    Value what went into it.

    Food carries the water, land, energy, and work used to grow, prepare, and deliver it. Preventing waste keeps more of that effort serving its purpose.

    03 / AFFORDABILITY

    A better-priced bite.

    Clear savings help students find a meal within reach. Cafe-set minimum prices keep the business side of the decision in view.

    THIS DEMO: FOOD MOVEMENT

    Follow the food.

    These counts follow the same day as the case and menus.

    A discounted sale is a sale of surplus stock. Retained food stays in the closing ledger; it is not automatically counted as waste prevented. Transfers and discards are tracked separately.

    WHAT A CAMPUS PILOT WOULD MEASURE

    Measure the change.

    Compare unsold quantities and weighed food waste before and during a pilot, accounting for how much food the cafe prepared. Track student savings, cafe revenue, and where remaining food goes.

    Water and carbon estimates would need a documented method, product-specific data, and a credible baseline. The demo does not turn each sale into an assumed carbon saving.

    The Cafe Desk

    Your cafe, your day. Set it up here and watch it run on every screen.

    Start with your hours and menu, then set customer traffic and pricing rules. Schedule a food bundle or market crash in Pricing & Offers. Apply updates the display, mobile menu, and case together. Inventory and hours rebuild the demo at the current time; Restart returns to opening, paused.

    01: Hours & Day
    CAFE HOURS

    Set the Day

    Opening and closing times set the shared timeline. Adjust rush times below to fit your hours.

    02: Menu & Opening Stock

    Edit names, tickers, availability, opening quantities, and prices. Applying the plan rebuilds the day at the current time with these values. Turn a food off to remove it from both menus. Minimum price protects your price floor.

    03: Traffic & Rushes

    Set normal hourly purchases for each channel, then choose when rushes begin and how much traffic increases. A 2× multiplier doubles both rates. Orders use available stock and current prices.

    RushStart TimeDuration (Min)Rate Multiplier

    04: Pricing & Offers

    Set how often prices are reviewed and how far they can move. Your minimum prices and sale costs still apply. Applying rules replays the cafe plan to the current time.

    Prices never exceed the regular price. Maximum discounts remain within 45% and each review within 5%. New offers stop five minutes before closing.

    Scheduled Offers

    Save an offer for the day or launch it now. Food Bundles combine two items at their current prices. A Market Crash highlights price drops within your pricing rules. Both appear under Move the Market and on the menus.

    05: Live Stock & Review

    Fresh Stock

    A fresh batch keeps the existing stock and its price history intact.

    Food & Inventory

    OFFER REVIEW

    Review a Price

    Demo checkout

    Choose a batch and check its offer. Preview and publish the next price adjustment to every screen. A hold keeps the current price. Prices update at your configured review interval and can rise as purchases reduce stock. Newly received food is a separate batch.

    Evaluate to inspect stock pressure, time, and the next price. No recommendation changes the screen before acknowledgment.

    Advanced assumptions & stock set aside

    These are explicit prototype assumptions, not validated cafe economics or demand. Selling fees, contribution, and review limits are set in Pricing Rules. Each food has its own incremental sale cost and minimum price. No real checkout is connected.

    Configured rules allow up to 45% off regular price and at most 5% per adjustment. Purchases affect the next scheduled evaluation. The floor covers fees, incremental cost and required contribution. Prices never exceed regular price; offers withdraw five minutes before closing.

    MARKETBITE ALERTS

    Good Deals.
    Right on Time.

    A timely deal can turn a passing thought into a cafe visit. MarketBite alerts encourage students to stop by and buy surplus food at a lower price before it goes to waste.

    Follow the Price

    Price-drop and Closing Rush notifications point students to current offers. The menu updates with the same prices and availability, so students can check the deal before heading over.

    A Better Bite. Less Left Behind.

    For students, it’s a more affordable bite. For cafes, it’s a chance to sell food that might otherwise be left behind—and make better use of the water, energy, and work that went into it.
